correctness.rationale: For any equal-census positive abundance triples, majorization comparison gives a fixed rarefaction order by discrete convexity of j↦binom(N−j,m). For incomparable triples, after sorting and interchanging, a>A and c>C, and signed abundance counts have three ordered blocks of first-cumulative support. Twice summation by parts produces H_m=Σ_j G_j binom(N−j−2,m−2), with G_j sign pattern negative then positive. The binomial kernel has the reverse-monotone-likelihood-ratio cross product for j1<j2,m1<m2 (higher depths favor lower abundance index), so its negative/positive contribution ratio is monotone; hence H_m has at most one sign change. Independent exact rational check: for x=(6,2,2) vs y=(5,4,1), (R_2,R_3,R_4,R_9) are x=(73/45,61/30,163/70,3), y=(74/45,41/20,242/105,29/10). The crossing at m=3→4 proves sharpness. The source verifier fully enumerates profiles through N=35 and verifies binomial-kernel minors; the proof covers every finite N without reliance on finite enumeration.

value.rationale: An exact no-return principle for three-species richness rankings answers a concrete ecological comparison question in the first nontrivial equal-richness case; a sharp crossing witness and two-depth certificate make the all-census theorem useful. The variation-diminishing abundance constraint is not an elementary sample table recomputation and does not follow from knowing that crossings can happen.
